newsitem.title: FRANCE: French stocks open lower on Wall St blues.
newsitem.headline: French stocks open lower on Wall St blues.

text.p: French shares shed some of Tuesday's sharp gains at the opening, following losses overnight on the Dow Jones index.
But traders said they were not too worried about the Paris market which needed a pause after recent strong advances, and the continued strength of the dollar provided support.
The blue-chip CAC-40 index was down 14.74 points or 0.59 percent at 2,468.02 at 0927 GMT while the CAC-40 futures contract was down 16 at 2,468 from Tuesday's close.
Oil major Total bucked the trend as 1996 net income came in at 5.6 billion francs, which was at the upper end of forecasts.
Bouygues climbed after reporting 1996 net attributable profit of 650 million francs. Breakeven at the property division was welcome news, one broker said.

Cerus was among the most active stocks after reporting 1996 net attributable profit of 1.21 billion francs and a 110 franc per share special payout made possible by its Valeo stake sale last year. The payment was 10 francs more than expected.
